title: What is GDP?
examples: How is GDP calculated using different methods?
Does GDP tell us everything about a country's wealth?
What does 'per person' mean when talking about GDP?

explain.say: Today we are learning about measuring an economy. GDP helps us see the total value of goods and services.

items: GDP measures final goods and services.
It covers a specific time period.
It is calculated within a country's borders.

explain.say: The first way to measure GDP is by spending. We add up all spending by households, businesses, and government.
Next, we look at per person GDP. This divides the total GDP by the country's total population.
Per person GDP gives a better idea of the average standard of living. It helps compare living standards.

draw.text: Per Person GDP: Average living standard

explain.say: A real-life example is comparing two cities. The one with higher per person GDP might have a higher average income.

draw.text: Example: City A vs City B income

explain.say: A common mistake is forgetting to subtract imports from exports. This makes the total spending look too high.

faq.a: GDP measures the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given time period. It is a measure of economic activity, not overall happiness.
asks: How do I calculate the size of an economy?
Is GDP the only thing that matters for a country?

faq.q: Why do we use 'per person' GDP?
faq.a: Using per person GDP gives a more accurate picture of the average wealth or standard of living for the people living there. It adjusts for the total population size.
asks: Does per person GDP account for population growth?
What does dividing by population tell us?

faq.q: Does GDP measure everything a country has?
faq.a: No, GDP does not measure things like environmental health, leisure time, or the distribution of wealth. It only counts market transactions.
asks: What does GDP ignore about a country?

faq.q: What is the difference between Gross Domestic Product and Gross National Product?
faq.a: GDP measures production inside a country's borders, regardless of who owns the assets. GNP measures the total income earned by a country's citizens, regardless of where they are.
asks: Where does GDP look for production?
Does GDP care where the money comes from?

faq.q: If a country has high GDP but high poverty, what does that mean?
faq.a: It means the total economic output is high, but the wealth is not spread out evenly among the population. This points to inequality issues.
asks: What else should we look at besides GDP?

facts: GDP measures the total value of final goods and services.
It is calculated using spending, income, or production methods.
Per person GDP is found by dividing total GDP by the population.
GDP does not account for non-market activities like volunteer work.

quiz.say: If a country's total spending is one trillion dollars and it has ten million people, what is its per person GDP?
quiz.why: You divide the total spending by the number of people to find the average.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you multiply the two numbers together.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you divide by one hundred instead of ten million.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you forget to divide by the population.

quiz.say: Which component of spending includes money spent on new factories and machinery?
quiz.why: Investment refers to spending by businesses on capital goods, like machinery.

wrong.0: Consumption is spending by households on everyday items.
wrong.1: Government spending is on public services like roads and schools.
wrong.2: This measures trade between countries, not business spending.

quiz.say: If a country buys many goods from another country, which part of the spending calculation must be adjusted?
quiz.why: Imports are subtracted in net exports because they are not produced domestically.

wrong.0: Government spending is on public services, not trade adjustments.
wrong.2: Consumption is for goods and services used by people.
wrong.3: Investment is for new capital goods within the country.
